newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end up, outlook seen mixed.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end up, outlook seen mixed.

text.p: ** Pro-market budget-inspired stocks rally seen holding
ground, outlook mixed
** Budget seen widely accepted, improves political
stability-traders
** UBS Securities says "overweight" on Indian stocks;
Banque Paribas goes "neutral" from "buy"
** Late rally takes Bombay benchmark index up 1.9 percent at
provisional close
Bombay share prices shrugged off lethargy to close higher on Tuesday after a market-friendly budget was seen helping political stability, brokers said.
The 30-share Bombay Stock Exchange index finished 73.68 points, or 1.90 percent, higher at a provisional 3,944.73.

"The budget has been applauded by industrialists, the markets and the common man," said Vijay Pandya, director at Classic Share and Stock Brokers. "It has given new confidence in the government...its tenure looks secure."
There had been doubts whether the 15-party fractious government elected last May would complete its 5-year term.
"Easing liquidity and the abolition of tax on dividend income has significantly increased the attractiveness of investments in equities," UBS Securities said.
"We expect the stock market to rerate strongly as investors shift from debt to equities."
The investment arm of Union Bank of Switzerland said it recommended investors to go "overweight" on Indian stocks following Friday's 1997/98 (April-March) budget from "neutral".
But the international equity research division of Banque Paribas cautioned investors to stay "neutral" as the Indian market was overheated.
"We think the improvements overall are relatively small to have generated a 14 percent rise in the index in three days," it said. "We are getting nervous."
The BSE hit 4,007.91 intraday high on Monday before closing at 3,871.05 -- against 3,474.79 in pre-budget trade on Friday.
"We think this is a feeding frenzy and do not expect the market to hold at much over 4,000 at best," Banque Paribas said.
Classic's Pandya said the 30-stock index did not reflect the market's state.
"There're so many side counters (shares) that haven't moved. There're several good pickings for the smart investor," he said.
--RANJIT GANGADHARAN, Bombay Equities +91-22-265-9000
